instruction: Replace order-invariant segment averaging with an order-aware alternative; investigate RNN/LSTM and recommend options.
scope: Order-aware, checkpoint-compatible pooling for short segments of frozen contextual speech features.
sub_questions: What temporal information does mean pooling remove?
Which span encoders are suitable for roughly four-frame segments?
How can existing mean-pooled decoder checkpoints remain exact warm starts?
Which controls isolate order information from parameter count and retraining?

papers.title: Deep Sets
papers.method: Permutation-invariant functions built around commutative aggregation.
papers.results: Provides a characterization and practical architecture for set-invariant functions.
papers.relevance: Formal basis for why mean cannot distinguish a reversed fixed-vector sequence.

papers.title: Long Short-Term Memory
papers.problem: Decaying error flow in recurrent sequence learning.
papers.results: Improved learning on synthetic long-lag tasks.
papers.relevance: Foundation for an LSTM span encoder, though long memory is not needed for four-frame spans.

papers.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
papers.method: Introduces a gated recurrent unit in an encoder-decoder.
papers.results: Learned phrase representations improved the SMT setup studied.
papers.relevance: Supports GRU as the lighter recurrent prototype.

papers.title: Segmental Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.authors: Lingpeng Kong, Chris Dyer, Noah A. Smith
papers.problem: Joint modeling of sequence segmentations and segment labels.
papers.method: Bidirectional RNN encodings of the constituent tokens in each segment with a semi-Markov model.
papers.results: Reported gains on handwriting recognition and Chinese segmentation/POS tasks.
papers.relevance: Closest general precedent for an order-aware segment embedding.

papers.title: Segmental Recurrent Neural Networks for End-to-End Speech Recognition
papers.authors: Liang Lu, Lingpeng Kong, Chris Dyer, Noah A. Smith, Steve Renals
papers.problem: End-to-end acoustic modeling with latent segments.
papers.method: RNN feature extraction integrated with a segmental CRF.
papers.results: Reported 17.3 percent TIMIT PER in first-pass decoding.
papers.relevance: Direct speech precedent for recurrent segment features.

papers.title: Why and when should you pool? Analyzing Pooling in Recurrent Architectures
papers.authors: Pratyush Maini, Keshav Kolluru, Danish Pruthi, Mausam
papers.problem: Understanding pooled versus terminal recurrent representations.
papers.method: Gradient-flow and positional-bias analyses across text classification tasks.
papers.results: Pooling aided early gradient flow; terminal BiLSTMs were biased toward sequence endpoints.
papers.relevance: Supports retaining mean as a residual base instead of a pure final-state replacement.

papers.title: A Cross-Task Analysis of Text Span Representations
papers.problem: Choosing a representation for arbitrary spans.
papers.method: Six span representations, eight pretrained encoders, and six tasks.
papers.results: The best representation varied by task; the choice mattered more with fixed encoders.
papers.relevance: The frozen SSL setting needs a controlled ablation rather than an assumed winner.

papers.title: Named Entity Recognition as Structured Span Prediction
papers.authors: Urchade Zaratiana, Nadi Tomeh, Pierre Holat, Thierry Charnois
papers.problem: Span representation and structured decoding for NER.
papers.method: Compares endpoints, max pooling, convolution, and other span features.
papers.results: Endpoint representations were robust across tested models and datasets.
papers.relevance: Motivates a cheap ordered endpoint residual.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.results: Strong machine translation quality with greater training parallelism.
papers.relevance: Shows that a tiny attention pooler needs within-segment position information.

papers.title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks
papers.method: Permutation-equivariant attention blocks and invariant pooling by multihead attention.
papers.results: Competitive set-modeling results with an inducing-point linear-complexity variant.
papers.relevance: Negative control: attention without position can still ignore order.

papers.title: Attentive Statistics Pooling for Deep Speaker Embedding
papers.authors: Koji Okabe, Takafumi Koshinaka, Koichi Shinoda
papers.problem: Pooling frame features into speaker embeddings.
papers.results: Reported relative EER reductions of 7.5 and 8.1 percent on two evaluations.
papers.relevance: Shows learned statistics can help, but content-only weighted statistics remain order-invariant.

papers.title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning
papers.problem: Parallel sequence modeling as an alternative to recurrent networks.
papers.results: Reported substantially faster training and improved MT quality over its deep LSTM comparison.
papers.relevance: Supports a parallel temporal-convolution fallback if RNN packing is slow.

papers.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations
papers.authors: Alexei Baevski, Yuhao Zhou, Abdelrahman Mohamed, Michael Auli
papers.method: Contrastive learning over masked latent speech with a context network.
papers.relevance: The vectors being pooled already carry contextual information.

papers.title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
papers.venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing
papers.method: Masked prediction and denoising with a Transformer using gated relative position bias.
papers.results: Reported broad gains across SUPERB and representative speech tasks.
papers.relevance: The decoder-side input already mixes temporal context and position before pooling.

themes: Commutative pooling cannot itself represent within-segment order.
Recurrent segment embeddings are established, including in speech.
A mean-plus-zero-initialized residual preserves checkpoint behavior and pooling optimization benefits.
Short contextual spans favor endpoints or a small BiGRU before an LSTM or Transformer.

gaps.statement: No retained work tests order-aware pooling for four-frame segments of frozen WavLM features feeding an autoregressive text decoder.
gaps.evidence: p4 and p5 use recurrent segment encoders in different segmental models; p13 and p14 establish contextual speech inputs but not this pooling comparison.

gaps.statement: It is unknown whether gains come from order, extra parameters, or decoder retraining.
gaps.evidence: p7 finds task-dependent representation effects; a within-segment shuffle control is absent from this project.

gaps.statement: Order-aware pooling may interact with learned boundary error by emphasizing inaccurate endpoints.
gaps.evidence: p8 supports endpoints in clean text spans, while the project uses predicted acoustic boundaries.
